files.why: Add the search Input (existing @shared/ui/input primitive) bound to the composable's query ref and render the filtered rows instead of the raw list.
Own the query ref, debounce it via the existing @shared/lib/useDebounce, and expose a filteredInvoices computed built from a core predicate.
Add a pure, framework-free matchesInvoiceQuery predicate — which invoice fields are searchable is a billing domain decision, and core already houses invoiceTotalMinor/summarize.
Add the same search Input bound to the composable query and filter the rendered appointment cards (markup duplicated here, not promoted — rule 7, only two usages).
Own the query ref, debounce via @shared/lib/useDebounce, and expose a filtered appointments computed using a core predicate.
Add a pure matchesAppointmentQuery predicate — the searchable-field decision is scheduling domain logic, sitting beside findConflicts/durationMinutes.
Cover the new matchesInvoiceQuery predicate; core rules are unit-tested here already.
Cover the new matchesAppointmentQuery predicate alongside the existing scheduling core tests.

uncertain: Placing the match predicate in core/rules.ts vs. inlining it in the ui composable. I chose core because it is pure and 'which fields are searchable' is a domain decision (passes the 'delete Vue and it still makes sense' test, mirrors findConflicts/invoiceTotalMinor), but it is borderline enough that a reviewer could call it trivial UI-level string matching that belongs in the composable.

No new shared SearchInput component: rule 7 says promote only at 3+ same-reason usages, and this is exactly two, so I duplicate the Input+binding markup in each view. If the team expects a shared wrapper anyway, that would add a apps/web/src/shared/ui/... file (and must stay domain-noun-free).

Whether 'both list views' means InvoiceListView.vue and DayView.vue. Billing has one obvious list; scheduling's only list is DayView (a single-day schedule, not a generic list), so I assumed that is the second one.

Whether server-side filtering is intended. Both views currently load the entire list client-side (billing via the Pinia cache store, scheduling by fetching all appointments then filtering by day), so filtering-as-you-type never touches the server and 'without hammering the server' is satisfied purely by debouncing keystrokes. If real server-side search is wanted, the touched files change substantially (see questions).
questions: Client-side or server-side search? Today the full lists are already in memory, so a debounced client-side filter hits the server zero times. If you actually want a server query per search, we'd instead add a search param to data/queries.ts (and billing's store.ts / dto.ts, possibly each slice's index.ts) and debounce the fetch — a different, larger change.

What should each box match? For invoices: number only, or also status / client? For appointments: DayView currently shows resourceId, time and status but not clientId — should search cover resource, status, client id, or something human-readable we don't yet display?
Expected debounce delay (useDebounce defaults to 300ms) and desired empty-state / clear behaviour when no rows match?
Is keeping the search box duplicated across the two views (rather than a shared primitive) acceptable per rule 7, or do you want it promoted to shared/ui now in anticipation of more list views?
